name: Passive Layers Can Shield Only Nearby Overlap Corners
statement: Let a cornerless ample two-layer family have overlap $B$, and suppose every concept exclusive to one wing has the same restriction $\sigma_b$ on a passive coordinate set $Z_b$. Then every corner $v$ of $B$ has passive Hamming distance at most one from $\sigma_b$. If the distance is one with unique differing coordinate $z$, its exclusive shield is forced: $v^{\oplus z}$ belongs to that wing's exclusive part. Thus a corner at passive distance at least two becomes a corner of the full family, while a distance-one corner has only one possible exclusive neighbour.
proof: At passive distance at least two, $v$ has no exclusive neighbour. All horizontal directions at its copy belong to the unique maximal cube of $B$ through $v$, and the vertical edge joins the two copies, so all incident directions lie in the single product cube over that maximal cube. The copy is therefore a corner of the full family, a contradiction. At distance one the same argument forces an exclusive neighbour. Since every exclusive concept has passive word $\sigma_b$, adjacency can change only the unique differing coordinate $z$; hence the neighbour must be $v^{\oplus z}$.
